en: any of the small changes or levels that something is divided into; the process or result of something changing gradually
ex: gradations of colour
各种层次的颜色

en: a mark given in an exam or for a piece of school work
ex: She got good grades in her exams.
她考试成绩优良。

zh: a place where a road crosses a railroad at the same level (not on a bridge)
en: a place where a road crosses a railroad at the same level (not on a bridge)

zh: （美国教育体制中学生在某一时期内各科成绩的）平均积分点，平均成绩点数
en: the average of a student’s grades over a period of time in the US education system
ex: The law school required a minimum grade point average of 2.6 (on a 4.0 scale).
该法学院要求平均最低成绩为2.6（4.0分制）。

en: (in the US) a school for children between the ages of about 6 and 12
arranged in order or in groups according to difficulty, size, etc.
ex: graded tests for language students
语言学习者的分级测验

en: a student who is in the grade mentioned
ex: The play is open to all seventh and eighth graders.
所有七、八年级的学生均可观看此剧。

zh: （尤指公路或铁路的）坡度，斜率，倾斜度
（温度、压力等的）变化率，梯度变化曲线
en: a slope on a road or railway; the degree to which the ground slopes
ex: The route includes some steep gradients.
该路线包括一些陡峭的坡度。

en: the activity of checking and correcting the written work or exam papers of students
ex: There is some concern that grading is not always fair.
有人担心打分并不总是公平的。

en: an instrument for measuring the angle of a slope
happening slowly over a long period; not sudden
ex: a gradual change in the climate
气候的逐渐变化

zh: （社会改革上的）渐进主义，渐进主义政策
en: a policy of slow steady change in society rather than sudden change or revolution

zh: （社会改革上的）渐进主义，渐进主义政策
en: supporting or following a policy of slow steady change in society rather than sudden change or revolution
ex: They advocate a gradualist approach to economic reform.
他们主张采取渐进的方式进行经济改革。

en: slowly, over a long period of time
ex: to gradually increase/decrease
逐渐增加/减少

zh: 大学毕业生；学士学位获得者
en: a person who has a university degree
ex: job prospects for graduates
毕业生的就业前景

zh: a graduate student at a university who is paid to help with teaching or research
en: a graduate student at a university who is paid to help with teaching or research
ex: Graduate assistants in the department work 20 hours per week on designated projects.
该系的研究生助理每周在指定项目上工作20个小时。

en: a part of a college or university where you can study for a second or further degree
divided into groups or levels on a scale
ex: graduated lessons/tests
分级课程／测验

en: the act of successfully completing a university degree, or studies at an American high school
ex: It was my first job after graduation.
那是我毕业后的第一个工作。

zh: 希腊的；希腊人的；希腊语的
en: Greek

zh: a form of wrestling in which those taking part are not allowed to hold each other below the middle part of the body
en: a form of wrestling in which those taking part are not allowed to hold each other below the middle part of the body

zh: （公共场所墙上等处的）涂鸦，胡写乱画
en: drawings or writing on a wall, etc. in a public place
ex: The subway was covered in graffiti.
地下通道里涂满了乱七八糟的图画和文字。
